translation:
Angelica (Dang Gui) one qian and a half, Chuanxiong eight fen, Chenpi eight fen, Pinellia (Banxia) one qian, wine-atractylodes (Cangzhu/白朮?) one qian, stir-fried Corydalis (Yuanhu) one qian, Trogopterus droppings (Wulingzhi) eight fen, Alpinia (Liangjiang) eight fen, Euodia (Wuzhuyu) six fen, Acorus (Shichangpu) eight fen, Cyperus (Xiangfu) one qian, Amomum (Sharen) one qian, Bitter Orange (Zhiqiao) eight fen, fresh ginger one slice. If pain is severe add Frankincense (Ruxiang) one qian, Myrrh (Moyao) one qian, Cinnamon (Rougui) eight fen, Aucklandia (Muxiang) six fen.
Grind all together to powder, mix with the medicinal decoction, take in two installments.
translator_notes: 心痛常痛=recurrent heart/stomach pain; this is a prescription-formula heading (plain ingredient list rendered literally).
unresolved: "酒芎" ambiguous (wine-processed Chuanxiong or Atractylodes); kept as wine-atractylodes/Chuanxiong.
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）

translation:
Dang Gui two qian, Chuanxiong one qian, wine-Peony (Shaoyao) one qian and a half, Cyperus (Xiangfu) one qian, Amomum (Sharen) one qian, Atractylodes (Baizhu) one qian, wine-Scutellaria (Huangqin) one qian, Bitter Orange (Zhiqiao) eight fen, Euodia (Wuzhuyu) eight fen, Lindera (Wuyao) six fen, Cinnamon (Rougui) seven fen, Licorice three qian, fresh ginger one slice, red jujube three pieces.
If pain is severe add Liangjiang eight fen; if vomiting, add ginger juice and Pinellia (Banxia) one qian and a half; if distended, (add) areca peel (Dafupi) washed with wine one part; if thirsty, add Wumei one grain, washed free of smoke, decocted with the rest.
translator_notes: 有胎氣心痛=heart/stomach pain in pregnancy; plain ingredient-list formula rendered literally.
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）

translation:
Vexing emptiness (xufan), commonly named sudden irritation (baozhao); the left cun position, deficient and rapid, makes vexation of the heart. The left guan position, deficient and rapid, is cold of the gallbladder; meeting it after illness, the blood and qi are depleted.
The kidney water dried and exhausted also gives vexation and agitation; nourish yin and descend fire — do not doubt. Heart-vexation, seeing the signs, administer the good formula; gallbladder-cold, nothing surpasses Wendan Tang (Warm-the-Gallbladder Decoction).
Wendan Tang (Warm-the-Gallbladder Decoction) treats vexing emptiness; Erchen (Two-Matured) then gathers Zhuru (Bamboo Shavings) into it. Renshen (Ginseng) and Yuanzhi (Polygala) must be added; do not be like other channels, where one may end or cap off.
translator_notes: 左寸/左關=left cun / left guan pulse positions.
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）
